All four files exist in the tree. Owner is still "Athena". The measure names `cargo test -p xtask --test setup_one_command` and ends with `status: not shown`. The new test checks every one of these points, and it passed.

criteria.criterion: A new test file under xtask/tests/ (e.g. xtask/tests/setup_one_command.rs) parses docs/spec.toml and asserts OLY-B-A4-04 has a non-blank, non-`none` mechanism whose named files exist; asserts the owner; and asserts setup.sh has one locked `cargo run -p xtask -- setup` exec and a pinned, checksummed rustup-init.
criteria.evidence: I read xtask/tests/setup_one_command.rs. It deserializes docs/spec.toml and checks that the mechanism is not blank or `none`. It checks that the three required files are named and that every .sh, .rs or .toml token in the mechanism is an existing file, and it checks the owner and the measure. For setup.sh it checks: exactly one `exec ` line; that line is the last command and contains `cargo run`, `--locked` and `-p xtask -- setup`; a RUSTUP_VERSION= pin and the archive URL; four `sum=` checksums plus the comparison; and that the curl download comes after the `if ! command -v cargo` guard. These match setup.sh lines 8–29.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask --test setup_one_command`: it passes with the change. A test would fail if the mechanism were reverted to `none`, and the test asserts that case.

findings.summary: The change edits xtask/shard-timings.txt, which is not on the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: One line was added: `xtask --test setup_one_command 5.00`. The edit is required: xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs::checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit asserts that the timings file covers every test unit, so adding a test target without this line breaks that test. The deliverables list should have included it. The edit is harmless.

findings.summary: The test `reverting_the_mechanism_to_none_is_a_gap` only exercises the test file's own helper, `is_blank_or_none`. It never checks the gap rule the repository actually enforces.
findings.evidence: It sets a cloned entry's mechanism to none, "" or None and asserts the local helper returns true, so it is close to a tautology. It does not call the gap rule in xtask/tests/spec.rs. A simpler, more accurate approach: have the revert case go through the same function as spec.rs, or drop this test. `the_spec_entry_has_a_mechanism_owner_and_measure` already fails on the real file when the mechanism is `none`.

findings.summary: Some checks are loose substring checks.
findings.evidence: `main.contains("already installed")` and `fn gitleaks_present` only show that the strings exist, not that setup skips steps already done. Skipping is tested elsewhere, by setup_repeatable.rs (OLY-B-RUN-02), so this is acceptable.

summary: Pass. The candidate records `setup.sh` handing off to `xtask setup` as the mechanism for OLY-B-A4-04. It keeps owner Athena and writes a measure that names `cargo test -p xtask --test setup_one_command` and ends with `status: not shown`. The new test file reads the committed spec entry, setup.sh, rust-toolchain.toml, README.md and xtask/src/main.rs. It checks that the mechanism is not `none` and that every file it names exists; that setup.sh's single locked exec of `cargo run -p xtask -- setup` is its last command; that rustup-init is pinned, checksummed and downloaded only after the cargo-missing check; that the toolchain is pinned; and that the README documents ./setup.sh. I ran `cargo test -p xtask --test setup_one_command` (5 passed) and `cargo test -p xtask --test spec` (30 passed). Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. With the base entry (`none`) the spec-entry test would fail; I concluded that by reading the code, not by running it. There are two minor findings. First, xtask/shard-timings.txt is edited but not on the deliverables list; the edit is required by an existing ci_shards test. Second, the revert-to-none test only checks the test file's own helper. Setup behavior is unchanged, and docs/decisions.md and records/ are not touched.
